key_insight: Reducing memory to delayed feedback enables optimistic online optimization with time-varying constraints and guarantees that adapt to environmental change and prediction accuracy.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports stateful online learning and non-stochastic control under budget constraints, using potentially unreliable predictions to improve performance.
method: Reduce memory effects to delay by treating state-dependent gradients as delayed feedback.
Use optimistic updates that incorporate untrusted predictions.
Bound dynamic regret and cumulative constraint violation using path length and prediction accuracy.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical guarantees, not empirical evaluation: perfect predictions yield O(1) regret, with constraint violation O(√T) for unknown path length or O(log T) when path length is known or online observable.
watch_item: The stronger constraint-violation guarantee depends on knowing or observing path length online, which may be difficult in deployment.
paper_title: Dynamic Optimistic Constrained OCO with Memory via Delay Equivalence
